sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Smyrna, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Smyrna is a town of 63,321 people (Census estimate, July 1, 2025) in Rutherford County, in the Nashville metropolitan area. The population is up 19.2% from the April 2020 base and up from 39,974 at the 2010 census, so most of its housing is newer than what you find in older Tennessee county seats. The town covers about 23 square miles, with part of Percy Priest Lake inside its limits and Stones River and Stewarts Creek as its main waterways.

The town grew around a rail station between Nashville and Chattanooga, and the Sam Davis house is its main historic site. Sewart Air Force Base opened in 1941, and in 1983 the first vehicle left the Nissan plant, which now employs roughly 8,400 people. Buyers who work at Nissan, the airport or the Guard base often shop close to the plant, which keeps demand steady for houses in the 20-minute commute range.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Smyrna homeowners?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts lists a median owner-occupied value of $358,300 for 2020 to 2024, with 57.4% of homes lived in by their owners. Median gross rent is $1,461, and 20,226 households average 2.79 people each, a family-sized figure. Median household income is $81,926 in 2024 dollars.

  • Foreign-born residents: 18.1%
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree: 27.8%
  • Mean commute: 26.3 minutes
  • Residents under 18: 25.0%

With a younger, larger household mix than much of the state, many Smyrna buyers need three or four bedrooms and a fenced yard. Those are the features to photograph first. Numbers are from Census QuickFacts for Smyrna.

sections.h2: How much property tax does a Smyrna house carry?
sections.html:
Smyrna taxpayers get a single bill from the Rutherford County Trustee that combines town and county levies. The table shows the rates the Trustee lists for 2025 and what they mean for a house at the Census median value.

Item2025 figure
Rutherford County rate$1.8762 per $100 assessed
Town of Smyrna rate$0.5257 per $100 assessed
Combined rate$2.4019 per $100 assessed
Assessed value of a $358,300 home (25%)$89,575
Estimated annual billabout $2,151

The combined rate and the bill estimate are my arithmetic from the Trustee's FAQ. Your 2026 bill may carry a different rate, so read it for the figure the Trustee actually applied.

sections.h2: When does Smyrna property tax come due and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
Bills are due the first Monday in October, and Rutherford County accepts payment without interest through the last day of February. The county gives no early payment discount. The tax year runs from January 1 to December 31, so a mid-year sale splits the bill by months owned.

The Trustee tells new owners to read the closing statement or ask the title company who is responsible, because unpaid tax keeps accruing against the parcel. If a mortgage company pays your tax, the bill is only a courtesy copy. Smyrna residents can pay at the Smyrna Trustee office, at the Murfreesboro office, online or by mail. Call 615-898-7705 for the Smyrna counter.

sections.h2: Can an older or disabled Smyrna owner get tax relief or a freeze?
sections.html:
Yes. For tax year 2026 the Comptroller lists Rutherford County's standard freeze income limit at $54,690, and Smyrna is one of the jurisdictions that has adopted the higher local option limit of $63,470. The state sets the filing window at 35 days past the delinquency date, which falls in April.

A freeze fixes the tax at the amount of the first qualifying year, so sellers who hold one should tell the buyer's title company before closing. If you think your appraisal is too high, the state schedule has the county Board of Equalization meeting from June 1, and a further appeal to the state board is due by August 1 or 45 days after the county board's notice, whichever is later.

sections.h2: Does Smyrna restrict short term rentals or repairs before a sale?
sections.html:
Smyrna's zoning ordinance bars renting a single detached dwelling, or any part of it, for less than three months. Once a tenant has stayed three months or more, later extensions can be shorter. The town may ask for the lease or agreement and can cite a violation after notice. A buyer who plans nightly stays will not find that route open.

Pre-sale repairs have their own rule. Homeowner permits are issued only where the owner lives, or plans to live, in the house. They are not issued when the work is for resale or lease, so a flip or a sale prep job needs a licensed contractor to pull the permit. The Building Safety Department at 315 S. Lowry Street handles permits, and additions or decks begin with a site plan sent to permits@townofsmyrna.org.

  • Interior remodels start with a pre-permit inspection, 615-355-5704.
  • Contractors need a state license, insurance proof and a town business tax license or release form.
  • A Certificate of Occupancy shows a structure passed inspection.

sections.h2: Is flood risk a factor in a Smyrna sale?
sections.html:
It can be. The Town Planner serves as Floodplain Administrator and the town posts FEMA flood map panels revised May 9, 2023. Zones starting with A or V are the high-risk areas, and a federally backed mortgage on such a property requires flood insurance. Zones B, C and X carry lower but real risk.

If your house sits near Stones River, Stewarts Creek or the lake shoreline, look up the panel before you list and have the zone ready for buyers. Any work in a floodplain needs a development permit from the Floodplain Administrator, reachable at (615) 355-5706, before it starts.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Rutherford County?
sections.html:
Rutherford County's register lists a recording fee of $5 per page with a $10 minimum, plus a $2 computer fund charge. On top of that, Tennessee imposes $3.70 per $1,000 of price on a conveyance. For a house at the Census median of $358,300 that tax is about $1,326.

Every deed must show the name and address of whoever prepared it. Your buyer's title company normally handles the filing, but confirm in the contract which side pays the tax, since the sale agreement controls it.

sections.h2: Which way of selling suits a Smyrna house?
sections.html:
A listing works well for a move-in ready house near the Nissan corridor. If the house needs work, has a tenant, or a deadline looms, a cash offer from a company that buys as-is can close once title is clear, without a buyer's loan approval. Compare the number in writing against what you would net after repairs, commission and carrying costs on a listing.

Whatever you pick, confirm the payoff on any mortgage, check that no town property maintenance liens are open, and set the closing date after your move so you are not paying for two homes.

faqs.q: Does a Smyrna seller get one tax bill or two?
faqs.a: One. The Rutherford County Trustee has collected the Town of Smyrna tax together with the county tax since October 2017, so a single bill covers both.

faqs.q: What is the Smyrna town property tax rate?
faqs.a: The Trustee lists $0.5257 per $100 of assessed value for 2025, on top of the county rate of $1.8762. Check your latest bill for the 2026 rates.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Smyrna house by the night?
faqs.a: Not under current zoning. The ordinance bars renting a single detached dwelling to any tenant for less than three months.

faqs.q: Can I pull a homeowner permit to fix up a house I am selling?
faqs.a: No. Homeowner permits require that the owner live, or plan to live, in the home. For work done for resale, a licensed contractor must pull the permit.

faqs.q: Where do I get a flood zone answer for a Smyrna house?
faqs.a: Call the Town Planner at (615) 355-5706, or check the FEMA panels the town posts online. A federally backed loan on a zone A or V property requires flood insurance.
